title: Gates fixed before the runs: six classifiers judged once on sealed decisions
request: A promotion gate for each decision classifier, written before any result, in the shape of the main product's R3: sealed cases, a margin over the rule, lower bounds, a cluster bootstrap by dataset, demotion bars; each verdict stored as evidence and never rerun on the same sealed set.
spec: A portable gate in dclab_core and a runner that reads each point's sealed set once, only when it matches its committed fingerprint, with the model its card describes; verdicts as evidence records.
plan: Write the gate with its thresholds and their reasons before any sealed read.
Review it before the run and fix what could let a sealed set be read twice or judged loosely.
Commit and push the gate, then run once.
Record every verdict, and what the run shows the gate cannot see.

decisions.decision: The gate was committed and pushed before the run, with dev's expected verdict for each point in the campaign manifest.
decisions.why: Git history then shows the gate came first, and the run reads as a test of stated expectations.

decisions.decision: A sealed set is spent under every gate version.
decisions.why: Otherwise a rebuilt model under a new version could be tuned on the same sealed decisions.

decisions.decision: Every lower bound is a bootstrap of whole table groups.
decisions.why: A table's decisions, and a table and its hidden-name twin, are not independent.

decisions.decision: Promotion needs a margin over the rule strictly above zero.
decisions.why: The rule is free and explainable; a model that only matches it adds nothing.

change: dclab_core/decision_gate.py (new; dclab-core 0.20.0), dclab_rnd/decision_gate_run.py (new), Makefile (make decision-gate), the campaign manifest and six verdicts in evidence/campaigns/decision_models_v1; tests/test_decision_gate.py (new); CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, the plan, the roadmap.

findings.defect: A new gate version could read a spent sealed set again.
findings.scenario: After a failure, a rebuilt model under decision_gate_v2 would be judged on the same sealed decisions.
findings.cause: A run was refused per point and gate version, not per sealed set.
findings.fix: A point whose sealed fingerprint was judged is refused under any version.

findings.defect: The first run would have broken the lab page's campaign test.
findings.scenario: A campaign folder without a manifest has no objective.
findings.cause: Results were written without the campaign manifest.
findings.fix: The manifest committed before the run.

findings.defect: Thresholds could move within one gate version.
findings.scenario: After some points were judged, an edited bar would judge the rest under the same name.
findings.fix: A test pins them, and the runner refuses a version whose stored thresholds differ.

findings.defect: Yes/no bounds were Wilson intervals over rows that include each table's twin.
findings.scenario: A recall near the bar would pass on an interval too narrow.
findings.cause: The margin was clustered by table, the other bounds were not.
findings.fix: Every gating bound is a bootstrap of whole table groups.

findings.defect: One stray answer of a class never true could sink macro recall.
findings.scenario: Five classes, one answer of a sixth: recall fell from 0.957 to 0.797.
findings.cause: Recall was averaged over every class seen, answered or true.
findings.fix: Recall over the classes in the truth, precision over the classes answered.

findings.defect: The sealed file was read twice and a partial run blocked the rest.
findings.scenario: Plain --yes stopped at the first judged point.
findings.cause: The fingerprint was recomputed from a second read; judged points raised.
findings.fix: One read; judged points are skipped with a message.

findings.defect: The gate passed a leakage model that misses one planted kind in every table.
findings.scenario: With names hidden, every exact-identity leak (the outcome as a sum of columns) was answered as not a leak.
findings.cause: The class check runs over True and False, not over planted kinds; and the state holds bands only, which cannot tell an identity from an honest number.
findings.fix: Recorded as the gate's limit; decision_gate_v2 adds no planted kind missed, and the rule's relation check stays beside the model.
findings.test: the verdict's bounds: recall 0.8333 with no width

outcome: Two of six classifiers passed their sealed gate (semantic_role and leakage_suspect); four failed as dev predicted. The leakage classifier's blind spot (exact identities with hidden names) shows what a band-only state cannot see.
lessons: Commit the gate and write the expected verdicts before the run: the run then tests stated expectations.
An interval with no width is a finding: the same error in every table means a kind the model cannot see.
Check by planted kind, not only by answer class: an aggregate can pass while one kind is always missed.
risks: Only generated tables; no blind labels yet.
A model that passed still must run beside the rule's relation checks.
